Chapter Five: The Limits of Human Love and the Need for Something Greater
As we move through all the different forms of love—affection, friendship, romance—you start to notice a pattern, don’t you? Each one brings joy, comfort, and meaning to life. But if you look a little closer, you’ll also spot their limits.
Even the strongest bonds have their moments of disappointment, misunderstanding, and sometimes, loss. Human love, for all its beauty, is actually pretty fragile.
Think about a family that’s weathered years of ups and downs. There have been times filled with laughter and others with anger—moments when loving each other felt effortless, and others when it felt almost impossible. Or imagine friends who slowly drift apart, not because of a big fight, but simply because life pulls them in different directions.
Even the most passionate romance can fade, leaving only memories behind.
These experiences can hurt. But they also show us something important: human love on its own just isn’t enough. It’s limited by fear, by pride, and by the simple reality that people are imperfect.
No matter how hard we try, we can’t always love as well as we want to. Sometimes, selfishness wins out. Old wounds resurface. And forgiveness? It can feel completely out of reach.
But here’s the thing—the limits of human love aren’t the end of the story. They actually point us to something deeper, a longing for a love that doesn’t fail—a kind of love that isn’t held back by weakness or fear.
And this is where charity, or selfless love, comes in. Imagine a love that gives without expecting anything back. A love that forgives, without keeping score. One that stands strong, even when everything else falls away.
Charity isn’t something we can just create out of thin air. It’s a gift—something that comes from outside ourselves. It’s the love that moves a parent to forgive their child over and over. Or the compassion that inspires someone to help a stranger. It’s what turns sacrifice into hope, and pain into something meaningful.
But let’s be honest—charity isn’t easy. It asks us to let go of our pride, to admit that we need help, and to open ourselves up to something greater than ourselves. It’s a love that costs us, that demands everything we have, but in return, gives us more than we could ever imagine.
In the end, it’s the only love that can truly heal the wounds left by all the others.
